diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $\tau:[0,\infty)\rightarrow [0,\infty)$ be such that $\tau(t)\rightarrow 0$ as $t\rightarrow\infty$ and $\dot{\tau}\leq 0$. 

    Then $\lim_{t\rightarrow\infty}\KL(\mu_t|\pi)=0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound in the lemma (and the one in lem:KL between dynamic and moving target) controls ∫ q_t (|x|^2+1) dx and the term c·τ(t) via a uniform-in-t second-moment bound for μ_t. The only source of such a bound is lemma:mu_t bounded moments, which requires μ_0 to have a finite 4th moment; lemma:bdd_2_moment (cited instead) concerns π_τ, not μ_t. Moreover, the bound is applied from t=0 with KL(μ_0|π_{τ(0)}), while the derivative formula of lemma_time_deriv_KL is only established on [t_1,t_2] with t_1>0 and KL(μ_0|π_{τ(0)}) may be infinite or μ_0 may have no density. None of these hypotheses appear in thm:continuous diffusion final convergence or cor:final convergence continuous, which impose conditions only on τ. (The lemma is also stated with '=' where the proof yields '≤'.)

failure_location.quote: Therefore, using \cref{lemma:bdd_2_moment,lem:KL between dynamic and moving target} the result follows.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypotheses that μ_0 has a finite fourth moment and KL(μ_0|π_{τ(0)})<∞ (or state the bound from a positive time t_1 using the Gaussian bounds on q_{t_1}), replace '=' by '≤', and cite lemma:mu_t bounded moments instead of lemma:bdd_2_moment.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the continuous-time bound and the convergence theorem are unsupported for arbitrary initial laws μ_0 (e.g. heavy-tailed μ_0 or μ_0 with infinite KL); the argument only supports them under unstated moment/finite-KL assumptions on μ_0 or after restarting the bound at some t_1>0.
issues.title: Continuous-time bounds silently require moment/finite-KL hypotheses on the initial law μ0 (and cite the wrong moment lemma)
issues.why_classification: A local addition of standard hypotheses (or a restart at t_1>0) restores every claim, rate, and the qualitative convergence conclusion without new arguments.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As shown in~\citep[Lemma 3.2]{cordero2025non}, the Eigenvalues of $\nabla^2 \log p_\tau(x)$ are bounded uniformly in $\tau$ and $x$ and, thus, the result follows.
then the path $(p_\tau)_{\tau\in[0,1]}$ \cref{eq convolution path} satisfies \Cref{Ass_drift}.

issues.failure_explanation: The derived expression for ∂_τ log p_τ carries a prefactor 1/(2(1-τ)), and the proof only bounds the bracket by c(|x|^2+1) uniformly; it never controls the 1/(1-τ) singularity, so no constant c uniform on [0,1] is obtained. The statement is in fact false: for the target N(m,1) with m≠0 (which satisfies all hypotheses of prop:convolution_ass), p_τ = N(√(1-τ) m, 1) and ∂_τ log p_τ(x) = -(x-√(1-τ)m)·m/(2√(1-τ)), which diverges as τ→1 for fixed x. Hence the quadratic-growth condition of Ass_drift cannot hold with a uniform c on the full range τ∈[0,1] as claimed.

failure_location.quote: There exists $c>0$ such that the density \cref{eq convolution path} satisfies for $\tau\in[0,1]$, $|\partial_\tau  U_\tau(x)| \leq c(|x|^2+1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the lemma and prop:convolution_ass to τ∈[0,τ̄] for τ̄<1 (with c depending on τ̄), as is already done for the dilation and DAZ paths, and require annealing schedules with τ(0)≤τ̄; the bracket is then controlled by the uniform Hessian bound and Lipschitz growth of ∇log p_τ.
issues.overall_effect: prop:convolution_ass, which asserts Ass_drift for the convolutional/annealed-Langevin path on all of [0,1], is false as stated; the convergence theorems therefore do not cover schedules with τ(0)=1 (as used in the experiments) for this path without further argument.
issues.title: Quadratic growth bound for the convolutional path fails uniformly on [0,1]: the 1/(1-τ) factors blow up as τ→1
issues.why_classification: The result must be weakened by excluding a neighbourhood of τ=1 (a limited but genuine scope loss for the advertised annealed-Langevin path); a recognizably comparable result survives without new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since by~\cref{lem_second moments of discretization remain bounded}, $\sup_k \E[ |X_{t_k}|^2]<\infty$,
We always pick the largest possible step size that the theoretical results allow for each method: $\step_k=\dissi_{\tau(t_k)}/\lip_{\tau(t_k)}^2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator 1-exp(-2h(a-L^2 h)) in the fixed point ŝ_k tends to 0 as h→a/L^2, so ŝ_k is not bounded merely because h_k is bounded and h_k<a/L^2. Counterexample with constant a,L: h_k=(a/L^2)(1-1/(k+2)) is bounded and strictly below a/L^2, yet 1-2h_k a+2L^2h_k^2 ≈ 1-2a^2/(L^2(k+2)), and the sum Σ_i h_i Π_j(...) grows like a linear function of k, contradicting the lemma's conclusion. Consequently the hypothesis eq step size condition of lem_second moments of discretization remain bounded is not implied by the hypotheses of lemma:discretization descent (only h_k<a_τ/L_τ^2 is assumed there), so the uniform bound sup_k E|X_{t_k}|^2<∞ used to obtain a k-independent constant c is unjustified.

failure_location.quote: Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:fixed point phi} is bounded for $h_k$ bounded (note that it converges to $1/(2\dissi)$ as $h_k\rightarrow 0$), it follows that $\sup_k \hat s_k\leq M<\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the step-size hypothesis to h_k ≤ (1-η) a_{τ(t_k)}/L_{τ(t_k)}^2 for some fixed η>0 (then ŝ_k ≤ C/(ηa) and the lemma's proof goes through), or, for corr discrete convergence, note that h_k→0 forces this eventually and finitely many initial steps have finite moments.
issues.overall_effect: The k-uniform constant in the one-step descent bound (and hence the discrete error bound, the convergence theorem as written, and the constant-step remark in rmk:interpretation of results) rests on a false lemma when step sizes may approach the threshold a_τ/L_τ^2.
issues.title: Step-size lemma lem:added-1 is false when h_k approaches a_τ/L_τ^2; uniform second-moment bound for the discrete scheme unsupported
issues.why_classification: A standard uniform-gap step-size condition (automatically satisfied for square-summable steps) repairs the lemma and all dependents with no loss of conclusion or rate.

lem:potential and partition are Lipschitz in time

diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists a constant $c>0$ such that $\left|\partial_\tau U_\tau(x)\right|\leq c(|x|^2+1)$ for any $x\in\R^d$ and $\tau \geq 0$.

issues.failure_explanation: The step bounding |exp(-(U_{τ2}-U_{τ1}))-1| by |U_{τ2}-U_{τ1}| holds only when U_{τ2}-U_{τ1} ≥ 0; when the difference is negative and of size c|x|^2|τ1-τ2|, the left side grows like exp(c|x|^2|τ1-τ2|), so the inequality is false and the integrand need not even be integrable against p_{τ1} without a smallness restriction on |τ1-τ2|. Separately, item 1 asserts the bound c_1|x|^2|τ1-τ2| although the assumption only gives c(|x|^2+1)|τ1-τ2|; the proof drops the +1 (the users of the lemma re-insert a constant term).

failure_location.tag: lem:potential and partition are Lipschitz in time

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State item 1 with c(|x|^2+1)|τ1-τ2|; prove item 2 via the derivative ∂_τ Z_τ = -∫ ∂_τU_τ e^{-U_τ} (bounded by the growth condition and uniform moments, as already done in lem:KL between dynamic and moving target) instead of the exponential inequality, or note Z_τ≡1 under the paper's normalisation.
issues.overall_effect: Item 2 of the lemma is not proved as written; its uses are in fact unaffected because the paper's normalisation U_τ=-log p_τ makes Z_τ≡1, and item 1 is used only in the corrected form c_1τ+c_2τ|x|^2, but the stated lemma is not established by its proof.
